text: Now Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and in time Amnon son of David fell in love with her.
Amnon became so obsessed that he made himself sick over his sister Tamar, since she was a virgin and it seemed impossible for him to do anything to her.
But Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, son of David's brother Shimeah, and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
Jonadab asked Amnon why he looked so haggard morning after morning, and Amnon admitted he was in love with Tamar, his brother Absalom's sister.
Jonadab told him to lie down and pretend to be sick, and when his father David came to see him, to ask that his sister Tamar be sent to prepare food where he could watch her and eat from her hand.
So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill, and when the king came to see him, Amnon asked that his sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in his sight so he could eat from her hand.
David sent word to Tamar at the palace, telling her to go to her brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him.
So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying down, took dough, kneaded it, shaped it into cakes in his sight, and baked them.
She took the pan and served them out before him, but he refused to eat and ordered everyone else out of the room, and they all left him.
Then Amnon told Tamar to bring the food into his bedroom so he could eat from her hand, and Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to Amnon in his room.
But as she brought them near for him to eat, he grabbed her and said, come, lie with me, my sister.
She answered him, no, my brother, do not violate me, for this kind of thing is not done in Israel; do not do this outrageous thing.

She told him she would carry her shame with her forever, and that he would become like one of the outrageous fools in Israel; better, she said, to just speak to the king, who would not refuse to give her to him.
But Amnon would not listen to her, and being stronger than she was, he overpowered her and raped her.
Then Amnon hated her with an intense hatred, greater than the love he had felt before, and he told her to get up and go.
She said to him that sending her away was a greater wrong than what he had already done to her, but he would not listen to her.
Instead he called his young servant and told him to put this woman out of his presence and bolt the door after her.
She was wearing an ornamented robe, the kind the king's virgin daughters wore, and the servant put her out and bolted the door behind her.
Tamar put ashes on her head, tore the ornamented robe she was wearing, put her hand on her head, and went away crying loudly as she went.

Her brother Absalom asked her whether Amnon had been with her, and told her to keep quiet for now since he was her brother and not to take it to heart; so Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.
When King David heard about all this, he was furious.
Absalom said nothing to Amnon, good or bad, but he hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar.
Two full years later, Absalom had sheepshearers working at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, and he invited all the king's sons to come.
Absalom went to the king and said his servants were shearing sheep, and asked whether the king and his servants would come along.
The king told Absalom that they should not all go, so as not to be a burden to him; and though Absalom pressed him, David would not go but blessed him instead.
Then Absalom asked whether, if not the king, at least his brother Amnon could come with them, and the king asked why Amnon should go with him.
But Absalom pressed him until he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

Absalom ordered his young men to watch for the moment Amnon's heart was merry with wine, and when he gave the word, to strike Amnon down and kill him, telling them not to be afraid since he himself was commanding them, and to be courageous and valiant.
So Absalom's young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded, and all the king's other sons got up, mounted their mules, and fled.
While they were still on the road, a report reached David that Absalom had struck down all the king's sons and not one of them was left.
The king got up, tore his clothes, and lay on the ground, and all his servants standing nearby tore their clothes too.

But Jonadab, Shimeah's son and David's nephew, said the king should not think all the young men, the king's sons, had been killed, since only Amnon was dead — this had been Absalom's plan ever since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
So Jonadab told the king not to take it to heart, thinking all his sons were dead, since only Amnon was dead.
Meanwhile Absalom fled; and the young man on watch looked up and saw a large crowd coming down the road from the hillside behind him.
Jonadab told the king to look, since the king's sons were coming, just as he, his servant, had said.
As soon as he finished speaking, the king's sons arrived and wept loudly, and the king and all his servants wept very bitterly too.
But Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, and David mourned for his son every day.
So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and stayed there three years.
And King David's spirit longed to go out to Absalom, since he had been consoled over Amnon's death.
